summary: T. R. V. Murti was a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later serving at Oxford (~1949–1952), Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1967), and McMaster University (attested 1982).
T. S. Devadoss specializes in philosophy and Indology. His career includes posts at the University of Madras, where he was attested in 1994 and served as professor as attested in 2008.

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held positions at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1972 and later as professor from 1984 to 1992.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as principal of The Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).
T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held a post at Osmania University (~1964–1968) and served as professor at the University of Mysore from ~1968 to 1994.

T. Venkatacharya specialized in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente and at the University of Toronto, where he served as professor in the Department of East Asian Studies (attested 1971).

Tadao Yoshikawa is a scholar in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1955–1965). He held positions at Hanazono University (~1967–1979), Kyoto University (professor, ~1984–2000), and Ryukoku University (professor, ~2000–2007).

Tadashi Inoue was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts, Bukkyo University, and Nara University (professor, ~1985–2004).

Tadashi Tani, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed doctoral studies at Waseda University under Yuichi Kajiyama and studied at Kyoto University (1995). He was a professor at Kochi College (attested 1996–2000) and later lectured at several universities.
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After earning his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978, he held posts at SOAS University of London as professor (attested 1987–1996) and reader (attested 2005).
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Ming-Wood Liu.

Taido Kitamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, holding academic posts at Shuchiin University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and held a post attested from 1994 to 1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Graduate Theological Union and studied under multiple traditional teachers. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (adjunct professor, attested 2006–2010) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).

Taiji Kuroda is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in 1976. He held assistant professorships at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1986) and Osaka Gakuin College (attested 1988).

Taijun Inokuchi specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987) at Ryukoku University, and representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He held posts at Japan Women's University and the University of Tokyo (1912; 1918–1930).
Taiken Kyuma is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Vienna by 1999. He served as an associate professor at Mie University, attested from 2002 to 2008.
Taiken Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Hiroshima University. He held an assistant professorship at Aichi Gakuin University, attested in 1991.
Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer, attested in 2015.
